chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him: How is it that the menstruating woman may take what is in the mosque, but may not place anything in it? He said: “The menstruating woman is able to place what is in her hand somewhere other than it, but she is not able to take what is in it except from it.”

key_terms.إِلَّا مِنْهُ: except from it; meaning only from the mosque itself
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, the legal setting discussed in the ruling
key_terms.تَأْخُذُ: she takes; removing something from the mosque
key_terms.تَسْتَطِيعُ: she is able; indicating practical ability as the basis of the distinction
key_terms.تَضَعُ: she places; putting something into the mosque
key_terms.فِي يَدِهَا: in her hand; what she is carrying

ai.seo_question: Why may a menstruating woman take something from the mosque but not place something in it?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal distinction regarding a menstruating woman and the mosque: she may take something from the mosque but may not place something into it. The reason given is practical necessity, since taking an item located inside the mosque can only be done from there, whereas placing an item can be done elsewhere.
